Questions.content: Why is the task "SolveForOmegaCubedOne" necessary if we are given that \(\omega^3 = 1\) and can directly use the known roots of unity for \(\omega\)? This task might be redundant. Consider focusing directly on substituting the known values of \(\omega\) (which are \(1, \omega, \omega^2\), where \(\omega = e^{2\pi i / 3}\) and \(\omega^2 = e^{-2\pi i / 3}\)) into the expression.
